project.brief:
Design and construct an extraordinary contemporary Caribbean waterfront estate in Saint Lucia with an estimated property value of US$25 million.

The property occupies a spacious waterfront site with ocean views and a gently sloping landscape.

Create a sophisticated luxury residence with approximately six generous bedroom suites, expansive living and entertainment spaces, a memorable entrance, exceptional indoor-outdoor connections, substantial terraces, a spectacular infinity pool and integrated tropical landscaping.

Develop a coherent architectural concept with impressive massing, coordinated building volumes, beautiful proportions, interesting elevations, sophisticated materials and an unmistakable luxury-estate presence.

You have creative freedom over the building composition, number of levels, architectural style, roof forms and overall arrangement.

Construct the complete, editable 3D exterior architecture rather than a small conceptual representation.

reasons: explicit currency selects one contextual value reference; no valuation inferred

terrain.approximation: Single flat ground plane Y=0; ground slabs rest on it. Gentle slope is not constructed.
terrain.policy: NEW GENERATION SITE POLICY: Always design on one level ground plane at Y=0. Do not emit set-terrain during generation, even for a hillside brief; disclose the temporary flat-site constraint. Place ground floor/deck slab bottoms at Y=0 and their walking surfaces at a consistent small positive datum (typically 0.2m). Doors and enclosure start at that walking surface. Coordinate water freeboard with the selected coping datum and basin depth; model pool perimeter and basin explicitly using plates/walls, never cover water with an unbroken deck. Upper floors and balconies must have explicit slabs and architectural support/attachments; a balcony element is ONLY a glass railing, never a floor. No unsupported elevated ground terraces or isolated plinths.
limitations: No accurate site grading, terrain-following foundations, retaining structures, drainage or shoreline/bathymetric model is established.
Waterfront orientation, views and architecture may be designed, but a marketing description or scenic name is not terrain evidence.
The unchanged original brief still requests a gentle slope; the existing higher-priority generation policy explicitly requires disclosing the approximation.
